docs.title: Tally
docs.text:
Tally is tiny web analytics you host yourself. One script under 2 kB, no cookies, and one SQLite file for all your data.

  • Small: the tracking script is 1.8 kB gzipped and loads asynchronously.
  • Private: no cookies, no fingerprinting, and IP addresses are never stored.
  • Simple: one binary, one SQLite database, one dashboard.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
1. Install Tally on any server with Docker, or download the binary.

  2. Add the tracking script to your site:

    html <script defer src="https://stats.example.com/tally.js" data-site="example.com"></script>

  3. Open https://stats.example.com and log in with the admin password you set during install.

Page views show up within a few seconds. To count clicks, sign-ups or purchases, see Track events.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Tally is configured with environment variables.

Variable Default What it does TALLY_ADMIN_PASSWORD none, required Password for the dashboard TALLY_PORT 8080 Port to listen on TALLY_DATA /data Folder for the SQLite database and backups TALLY_RETENTION_DAYS 730 Raw events older than this are deleted; daily totals are kept forever TALLY_IGNORE_BOTS true Drop requests from known crawlers TALLY_PUBLIC false Make the dashboard readable without logging in

docs.title: Several sites
docs.text: One Tally server can track any number of sites. Each site is created the first time a page view with a new data-site value arrives; there is nothing to set up in advance.

docs.title: Excluding your own visits
docs.text: Open your site with ?tally=ignore once. Tally sets a flag in local storage and stops counting visits from that browser. Use ?tally=count to undo it.

docs.title: Track events
docs.text: Page views are counted automatically. Anything else, such as a button click or a sign-up, is an event.

docs.title: From JavaScript
docs.text:
Call tally.event with a name, and optionally a few properties:

tally.event("signup");
tally.event("purchase", { plan: "pro", value: 49 });

Event names are case-sensitive, up to 64 characters. Properties are strings or numbers, at most 10 per event.

docs.title: Without JavaScript
docs.text:
Add data-tally-event to any link or button, and Tally sends the event when it is clicked:

<button data-tally-event="download">Download</button>

docs.title: Goals
docs.text: In the dashboard, open Goals and pick an event to turn it into a goal. Tally then shows the conversion rate of each page and each referrer for that goal.

docs.title: Install
docs.text: Tally needs 64 MB of RAM and runs on Linux, macOS and Windows. A $5 VPS handles about 10 million page views a month.

docs.title: With Docker
docs.text:
docker run -d --name tally -p 8080:8080 \
  -v tally-data:/data \
  -e TALLY_ADMIN_PASSWORD=change-me \
  ghcr.io/example/tally:2

Put Tally behind a reverse proxy (Caddy, nginx) that handles HTTPS.

docs.title: As a binary
docs.text:
Download the latest release for your platform, then run:

TALLY_ADMIN_PASSWORD=change-me ./tally serve --port 8080 --data ./data

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text: Stop Tally, replace the image or binary, start it again. Database migrations run on start-up, and a backup of the database is written to data/backups/ first.

docs.title: Privacy
docs.text: Tally does not use cookies and does not store personal data, so in most cases you do not need a cookie banner for it. Check with your own legal advice if you are unsure.

docs.title: What is stored
docs.text: For each page view: the page path, the referrer's domain, the browser and operating system family, the country (looked up from the IP address, which is then thrown away), and the screen size class (phone, tablet or desktop).

docs.title: How unique visitors are counted
docs.text: Tally hashes the IP address and user agent together with a secret salt that changes every 24 hours. The hash lets Tally count a visitor once per day; after the salt changes, nobody, including you, can link a visit to an earlier one.

docs.title: Do Not Track
docs.text: Tally respects the Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control signals by default. Set TALLY_RESPECT_DNT=false to count those visitors anyway.
